answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a stake before its actions count, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. A sybil operator can mint keys cheaply, but cannot cheaply multiply voting weight: each new identity needs more capital held at risk, and colluding identities expose that capital to coordinated penalties. A shale-backed credit pool might fund honest newcomers, yet audits must prevent it becoming a trellis for laundering one attacker’s stake across accounts; at the nadir, the attacker still pays for every funded identity.
